stem:
Some of the common chlorides of Period 3 elements are shown in the list.

$\text{NaCl} \quad \text{MgCl}_2 \quad \text{AlCl}_3 \quad \text{SiCl}_4 \quad \text{PCl}_5$

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: all the chlorides that have giant ionic structures in the solid state

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: all the chlorides that react vigorously with water to form strongly acidic solutions

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: the chloride that dissolves in water to form a neutral solution

parts.label: (a)(iv)
parts.text: the chloride formed from the **element** with the highest melting point.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
$\text{NaCl}$ is one product of the reaction of chlorine gas and cold aqueous sodium hydroxide.

Identify the other products.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: $\text{PCl}_5$ reacts with alcohols to form chloroalkanes.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Draw the structure of the organic product formed in the reaction of an excess of $\text{PCl}_5$ with butane-1,3-diol.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Sulfur, $\text{S}_8$, reacts with chlorine to form several different chlorides. The most common are $\text{S}_2\text{Cl}_2$ and $\text{SCl}_2$. $\text{SCl}_2$ forms when sulfur reacts with an excess of chlorine.

reaction **1** $\text{S}_8\text{(s)} + 4\text{Cl}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow 4\text{S}_2\text{Cl}_2\text{(l)}$ $\Delta H_\text{r} = -58.2\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

reaction **2** $\text{S}_2\text{Cl}_2\text{(l)} + \text{Cl}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SCl}_2\text{(l)}$ $\Delta H_\text{r} = -40.6\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text:
$\text{SCl}_2$ is a cherry-red liquid that reacts vigorously with water to form an acidic solution.

Use this information to deduce the bonding and structure shown by $\text{SCl}_2$. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the enthalpy change of formation, $\Delta H_\text{f}$, of $\text{SCl}_2\text{(l)}$. You may find it useful to use Hess's Law to construct an energy cycle.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text: State the effect of a decrease in pressure on the position of equilibrium in reaction **2**. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (d)(iv)
(d)(v)
parts.text: Suggest a value for the $\text{Cl}-\text{S}-\text{S}$ bond angle in isomer **I**. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (d)(vi)
parts.text: Draw a dot-and-cross diagram to show the bonding in isomer **II**. Show outer shell electrons only.
